title: Legislative districts of Oriental Mindoro
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Oriental Mindoro''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Oriental Mindoro]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative districts of Mindoro}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Oriental Mindoro were represented under the [[Mindoro's at-large congressional district|lone district]] of the undivided [[Mindoro (province)|Mindoro Province]] from 1898 to 1951. The enactment of Republic Act No. 505 on June 13, 1950 split the old Mindoro Province into [[Occidental Mindoro]] and [[Oriental Mindoro]], and provided each of them separate representation in Congress.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=505|title=An Act to Create the Provinces of Oriental Mindoro and Occidental Mindoro|date=June 13, 1950|access-date=November 28, 2017|url=http://www.thecorpusjuris.com/legislative/republic-acts/ra-no-505.php}} Pursuant to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 505, the incumbent representative of Mindoro began to [[Legislative districts of Oriental Mindoro#Lone District (defunct)|represent only Oriental Mindoro]] in the second half of the [[2nd Congress of the Philippines|2nd Congress]], following the election of Occidental Mindoro's [[Legislative district of Oriental Mindoro#Lone District|separate representative]] in a [[List of special elections to the Philippine Congress#House of Representatives|special election]] held on the same day as the [[1951 Philippine Senate election|1951 senatorial elections]]. Oriental Mindoro was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV-A]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|two representatives, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province was reapportioned into two congressional districts;{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} each elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. == Current districts == {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative Districts and Congressional Representatives of [[Oriental Mindoro]] |- !District ! colspan="3" |Current Representative !Party !
